svg.title: Your file, the host, and the pipe between them
svg.desc: A host process on the left and the reader's Python server process on the right, drawn the same size, connected by three labelled streams. A dashed arrow at the top shows the host spawning the server once at startup with a uv command. Below it, standard input carries one JSON-RPC request per line from host to server, standard output carries the answers back and is marked as the protocol stream where a stray print would be parsed, and standard error turns downward out of the exchange into the host log file, which is collected and shown to you but never parsed. The host box lists Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or your own CLI and contains one client per connected server; the server box runs python dash m system underscore info and holds app.py with the MCPServer constructor and tools.py with a decorated function. A closing line says nothing here is a network: two processes, one pipe each way, and a third for everything that is not an answer.
svg.text: Your file is a child process, and three streams do all the work
There is no server to deploy and no port to open. The host starts your file and talks to it through pipes.
Started by the host, not by you.
Exits when the host closes the
A stray print() lands here and is parsed.
Collected, shown to you, never parsed.
Nothing here is a network. Two processes, one pipe each way, and a third for everything that is not an answer.
